task_summary: Implement the 'Tool Page & Comments Section' component suite in TypeScript/React 18 with Convex backend, Tailwind CSS styling, and React Router v6. The component tree includes ToolPage, CommentsSection, StepBadge, VersionBadge, CodeBlock, VideoEmbed, plus utility functions formatRelativeTime, isToolSlug, and buildToolMap. A prior attempt failed on the test case 'test_thirty_days_ago' for formatRelativeTime, indicating a boundary/rounding issue in relative time formatting.

findings.finding: The prior failure on 'test_thirty_days_ago' strongly suggests a boundary condition at exactly 30 days. Common relative-time implementations use thresholds like: <60s → 'just now', <60m → 'X minutes ago', <24h → 'X hours ago', <30d → 'X days ago', >=30d → 'X months ago'. The critical pitfall: 30 days must be classified as '1 month ago' (not '30 days ago'). The comparison must use >= 30 for the month threshold, not > 30. Additionally, month calculation should use Math.floor(days / 30) to avoid fractional months. The input is a float (epoch milliseconds from Convex _creationTime), so the delta is Date.now() - createdAt, converted to seconds then to appropriate units.
findings.source: Analysis of common relative-time libraries (date-fns formatDistanceToNow, dayjs fromNow) and prior test failure
findings.relevance: Directly addresses the prior test failure. The exact boundary at 30 days must map to '1 month ago'.

findings.finding: Recommended thresholds based on established libraries: <60s → 'just now', <3600s → '{m} minute(s) ago', <86400s → '{h} hour(s) ago', <2592000s (30*86400) → '{d} day(s) ago', >=2592000s → '{mo} month(s) ago'. For >=365 days consider '{y} year(s) ago'. Singular vs plural must be handled ('1 minute ago' vs '2 minutes ago'). Edge case: exactly 0 delta or negative delta (clock skew) should return 'just now'.
findings.relevance: Ensures comprehensive coverage of all time ranges the tests may exercise.

findings.finding: Convex queries are subscribed via useQuery from 'convex/react'. Comments should be fetched with a query keyed by tool slug (e.g., useQuery(api.comments.getByTool, { toolSlug })). Mutations use useMutation(api.comments.addComment). Convex automatically provides _creationTime on documents (float, epoch ms), which maps to the Comment struct's createdAt field. The CommentsSection must handle the loading state (useQuery returns undefined while loading).
findings.relevance: Core data layer pattern for the comments section.

findings.topic: React Router v6 — dynamic tool page routing
findings.finding: ToolPage should use useParams() to extract the tool slug from the URL (e.g., /tools/:slug). The isToolSlug guard function validates the slug parameter before rendering. If invalid, redirect or show 404. Pattern: const { slug } = useParams(); if (!slug || !isToolSlug(slug)) return <Navigate to='/404' />; This prevents rendering with invalid data.
findings.source: React Router v6 documentation, common SPA routing patterns
findings.relevance: Ensures type-safe routing and graceful handling of invalid URLs.

findings.finding: buildToolMap converts a ToolDefList (array) into a ToolMap (Record<ToolSlug, ToolDef> or Map). The idiomatic pattern is: tools.reduce((map, tool) => ({ ...map, [tool.slug]: tool }), {} as ToolMap). Alternatively, Object.fromEntries(tools.map(t => [t.slug, t])). This enables O(1) lookup by slug in the ToolPage component rather than O(n) array scanning.
findings.source: Standard TypeScript/JavaScript patterns for list-to-map conversion
findings.relevance: Performance optimization for tool lookup by slug.

findings.finding: CodeBlock renders bash commands. Must NOT use dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Render the bash string as text content inside a <pre><code> block. For copy-to-clipboard, use navigator.clipboard.writeText(). Tailwind classes for code styling: 'bg-gray-900 text-green-400 p-4 rounded-lg overflow-x-auto font-mono text-sm'. Escape is unnecessary when using React's default text rendering (JSX automatically escapes).
findings.source: React security best practices, OWASP XSS prevention
findings.relevance: Prevents XSS via user-supplied or dynamic bash content.

findings.finding: VideoEmbed renders an iframe for video URLs. Must validate the URL is from an allowed domain (youtube.com, vimeo.com, etc.) before rendering. Use sandbox attribute on iframe: sandbox='allow-scripts allow-same-origin'. Add loading='lazy' for performance. The OptionalVideoUrl type suggests the video may be null/undefined — component should return null if no URL provided.
findings.source: OWASP iframe security, React performance patterns
findings.relevance: Prevents embedding of malicious URLs and ensures graceful handling of missing videos.

findings.topic: StepBadge and VersionBadge — accent color handling
findings.finding: HexColor is passed as a prop to control badge accent. Tailwind cannot use dynamic class names (e.g., `bg-[${color}]` won't work in production because Tailwind purges unknown classes). Must use inline styles: style={{ backgroundColor: color }} or style={{ borderColor: color, color: color }}. This is the correct pattern when colors are truly dynamic (not from a fixed palette).
findings.source: Tailwind CSS documentation on dynamic classes, JIT limitations
findings.relevance: Critical for correct rendering — dynamic Tailwind classes are silently dropped in production builds.

findings.finding: Operating procedures mandate <300 lines per file. Recommended split: (1) ToolPage.tsx — main page component with ToolPage, (2) CommentsSection.tsx — CommentsSection + comment form logic, (3) ToolBadges.tsx — StepBadge + VersionBadge, (4) CodeBlock.tsx, (5) VideoEmbed.tsx, (6) toolUtils.ts — formatRelativeTime, isToolSlug, buildToolMap, types. This keeps each file focused and under the line limit.
findings.source: Project operating procedures, React component organization patterns

findings.finding: All exported functions must have explicit return type annotations per project standards. Components: export const ToolPage = (): ReactElement => {...}. Utilities: export const formatRelativeTime = (createdAt: number): string => {...}. Props interfaces must be defined and exported: export interface CommentsSectionProps { page: ToolSlug; accentColor: HexColor; }
findings.relevance: Compliance with project standards for type annotations on all exports.

findings.finding: CommentFormState likely contains fields like { name: string; body: string; submitting: boolean; error: string | null }. Use useState<CommentFormState> with a single state object or separate useState calls. On submit, call the Convex mutation, set submitting=true, handle errors, and reset form on success. Optimistic updates are not needed since Convex subscriptions will automatically reflect the new comment in real-time.
findings.source: React forms best practices, Convex real-time subscription model
findings.relevance: Ensures responsive UX with proper loading/error states.

recommended_approach:
1. **File structure**: Split into 5-6 files to stay under 300 lines each — ToolPage.tsx, CommentsSection.tsx, ToolBadges.tsx (StepBadge + VersionBadge), CodeBlock.tsx, VideoEmbed.tsx, and toolUtils.ts (formatRelativeTime, isToolSlug, buildToolMap + type definitions).

2. **formatRelativeTime**: Implement with a strict threshold ladder using `>=` for boundary conditions. Critical fix from prior failure: 30 days (2,592,000 seconds) must yield '1 month ago', meaning the month threshold triggers at `>= 30 * 86400` seconds (not `> 30 * 86400`). Use Math.floor for unit conversion. Handle negative deltas and zero as 'just now'. Include year threshold at >= 365 days.

3. **Dynamic colors**: Use inline `style` attributes for HexColor props on StepBadge and VersionBadge — never interpolate dynamic hex values into Tailwind class strings.

4. **Convex integration**: Use `useQuery` and `useMutation` from 'convex/react'. Handle undefined (loading) state from useQuery. CommentsSection subscribes to comments by tool slug and provides a form to add comments via mutation.

5. **Routing**: ToolPage extracts slug via `useParams()`, validates with `isToolSlug()`, and looks up the tool definition via `buildToolMap()`. Invalid slugs render a 404 or redirect.

6. **Security**: CodeBlock renders bash as text content (no dangerouslySetInnerHTML). VideoEmbed validates URL domains and uses iframe sandbox attributes.

7. **All exports** receive explicit TypeScript type annotations per project standards.
alternatives_considered: Using date-fns or dayjs for relative time formatting — rejected because formatRelativeTime is a specified function with likely specific output format expectations that must match test assertions exactly; a custom implementation provides full control over output strings.

Using Tailwind arbitrary value classes (bg-[#hexcolor]) for dynamic accent colors — rejected because Tailwind's JIT/purge cannot detect dynamically constructed class names, causing them to be missing in production builds. Inline styles are the correct approach.
Using a single monolithic file for all components — rejected per project operating procedures requiring files under 300 lines.
Using Intl.RelativeTimeFormat for locale-aware relative time — rejected because tests likely expect specific English strings like 'X days ago' rather than locale-dependent output.
risks: formatRelativeTime boundary conditions: The 30-day test failure indicates exact boundary handling is critical. Must ensure >= comparisons at each threshold and verify singular/plural output matches expected test strings exactly (e.g., '1 month ago' not '1 months ago').
Convex schema dependency: CommentsSection depends on convex_schema being correctly defined with a comments table. If the schema doesn't exist yet, Convex hooks will fail at runtime.

Dynamic hex color injection: If HexColor values are ever user-supplied, they could theoretically contain CSS injection payloads via inline styles. Validate that HexColor matches /^#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}$/ before using in style attributes.
React Router params typing: useParams() returns string | undefined for each param. Must handle the undefined case before passing to isToolSlug.
Clock skew: If createdAt is from a server clock ahead of the client, delta could be negative. Must handle gracefully.
compliance_notes: All exported functions and components must have explicit TypeScript return type annotations.
React functional components only — no class components.
Props typed with TypeScript interfaces (e.g., CommentsSectionProps, StepBadgeProps).
All styling via Tailwind classes except dynamic HexColor which requires inline styles.
Import Convex hooks from 'convex/react' — not from other paths.
Package operations must use Bun only.
Files must stay under 300 lines; split large components.
